course.description.note: Back-translation check: 'Kajian sosial' is the agreed key term. The back-translator says it reads as a literal translation, not the name of a Malaysian school subject. Check that learners and partner staff find it natural.
course.description.back: A free social studies course with 24 lessons about history, geography, culture and civic life.
course.description.source: A free social studies course with 24 lessons about history, geography, culture and civic life.

sections.0.question.note: Back-translation check: The section questions use 'Bagaimanakah', which is correct but a little formal for children. Check whether 'Bagaimana' sounds more natural in all four section questions (sections.0–3.question).
sections.0.question.back: How have people, ideas and events shaped the world in which we live?
sections.0.question.source: How have people, ideas, and events shaped the world we live in?

sections.0.description.note: Translator: 'movement' is translated as 'perpindahan' (people moving or migrating). Check that it reads naturally here and doesn't sound like physical motion. Back-translation check: 'Movement' here means people moving or migrating. 'Perpindahan' is close but general. Check whether it reads as migration in this list, or whether 'penghijrahan' would be clearer for young readers.
sections.0.description.back: Explore how people, ideas, inventions, movement and trade have shaped the world.
sections.0.description.source: Explore how people, ideas, inventions, movement, and trade have shaped the world.

sections.1.question.back: How do places shape people's lives, and how do people shape places?
sections.1.question.source: How do places shape people's lives, and how do people shape places?

sections.1.description.note: Translator: 'resources' is translated as 'sumber' to match the glossary. Check that it isn't read as 'sources' here. 'sumber asli' is clearer but narrower. Back-translation check: 'Resources' uses the key term 'sumber', but in a list it could be read as 'sources'. Check whether 'sumber alam' is clearer here. If so, decide it across the whole site, not just in this row.
sections.1.description.back: Understand maps, places, resources, climate, cities and the relationship between people and the environment.
sections.1.description.source: Understand maps, places, resources, climate, cities, and the relationship between people and the environment.

sections.2.question.note: Back-translation check: 'Rasa kekitaan' is the agreed term for 'belonging'. The back-translator says it is a bit literary and abstract for younger learners. Check that 10 to 13-year-olds understand it.
sections.2.question.back: How do people create meaning, community and a sense of belonging?
sections.2.question.source: How do people create meaning, community, and belonging?

sections.2.description.back: Learn how communities create meaning through language, traditions, art, daily life and shared experiences.
sections.2.description.source: Learn how communities create meaning through language, traditions, art, everyday life, and shared experiences.

sections.3.question.note: Translator: 'resources' is translated as 'sumber' to match the glossary. Check that it isn't read as 'sources' here. Back-translation check: 'Use resources' uses 'sumber', which could be read as 'sources'. Check this together with sections.1.description and keep both the same.
sections.3.question.back: How do people make choices, use resources and build fairer communities together?
sections.3.question.source: How do people make choices, use resources, and build fairer communities together?

sections.3.description.note: Translator: 'media literacy' is translated as 'literasi media', which Malaysian schools use. Check that young readers will understand it. Back-translation check: Check two things. First, that young readers understand 'literasi media'. Second, 'belia' is the agreed term for 'youth', but in Malaysian policy it means people aged about 15 to 30 or 40. It may not fit 10 to 17-year-olds, so check whether 'remaja' or 'orang muda' would fit better.
sections.3.description.back: Explore everyday economics, media literacy and how youth can contribute to their communities.
sections.3.description.source: Explore everyday economics, media literacy, and how youth can contribute to their communities.

practiceOptions.0.note: Back-translation check: 'Dengan rakan' is the agreed key term, but it doesn't show that there was one partner. Check whether 'dengan seorang rakan' reads better here.

practiceOptions.3.note: Translator: 'with sign' is translated as 'dengan bahasa isyarat' (with sign language). Check this matches what was meant. Back-translation check: 'With sign' was translated as 'dengan bahasa isyarat' (sign language). Check that this is what was meant. Also check that 'secara senyap' reads as 'quietly' and not 'secretly'.
practiceOptions.3.back: I practise in another way (silently, with sign language or in writing)
practiceOptions.3.source: I practised another way (quietly, with sign, or in writing)
